connector: Hoo, hello! You’ve read five books this year: Mrs. Frisby and the Rats of NIMH, Anne of Green Gables, Number the Stars, Freedom Train and Prince Caspian. This week you put them side by side. A theme is a big idea a story keeps coming back to, and the best ones show up in more than one book. Pick one today.

a.raw: peter said to caspian i havent come to take your place you know but to put you into it
a.fixed: Peter said to Caspian, “I haven’t come to take your place, you know, but to put you into it.”
a.why: Peter’s real words (Prince Caspian, Ch. 12): capitals on Peter, Caspian and I; an apostrophe in haven’t; commas around you know; the period inside the quotation marks.

b.raw: this year we read five books and we kept a learning journal
b.fixed: This year we read five books, and we kept a learning journal.
b.why: Capital T to start; a comma before and joins two complete thoughts; a period ends it.

virtue.title: Which pillar is it?
virtue.intro: The OAO Seven Pillars are honesty, respect, courtesy, responsibility, courage, service and perseverance. These moments come from three books this year. Tap the pillar each one shows best.

items.t: Number the Stars: Uncle Henrik tells Annemarie, “That’s all that brave means — not thinking about the dangers. Just thinking about what you must do.”
items.why: Brave means doing what you must, even when you are afraid.
items.hint: What does Uncle Henrik say brave means?

items.t: Anne of Green Gables: Matthew says, “Well now, I’d rather have you than a dozen boys, Anne.”
items.why: He tells Anne she is valued just as she is.
items.hint: How does Matthew make Anne feel?

items.t: Prince Caspian: Peter tells Caspian, “I haven’t come to take your place, you know, but to put you into it.”
items.why: He uses his power to help Caspian, not to replace him.

notes.wordParts: Every base from the year: port, tract, struct, spect, ject, script, rupt, duct, form, press, tain, lev, plus prefixes like pre-, re-, trans-, inter-.
notes.grammar: Spiral review: capitals, commas, quotation marks, complete sentences. Read your sentence out loud and check each mark has a job.
notes.spelling: Spiral review: drop the silent e, change y to i, double the last consonant when the beat is on the last syllable, and spell each word part the same way every time.

morphology.label: Opti · a year of word parts

transcripts.welcome: Hoo, hello! It’s Opti. You’ve read five books this year, and now you get to put them side by side. Today’s question: what big ideas show up in more than one story?
transcripts.read: A theme isn’t one word on a page. It’s a big idea about life that a story keeps showing, like courage or belonging. Look at your reading shelf. Pick one theme, and find one character who shows it.
transcripts.morphology: You learned a lot of word parts this year. Port means carry. Spect means look. Rupt means break. Pre means before. When you meet a long word, find a part you know, and the word starts to explain itself.
